profile.headline: Robotics & Computer Vision | Caltech PhD
profile.summary:
I'm a PhD researcher at Caltech specializing in computer vision and robotics. My research focuses on developing robust and real-time perception algorithms for autonomous systems operating in challenging environments using visual and thermal sensors.

I've authored multiple publications in top robotics/CV conferences and journals (ICRA, IROS, Science Robotics, etc...) and co-created the first RGB-Thermal natural scenes dataset for advancing aerial field robot perception algorithms. Notably, my contributions have earned recognition, including a Best Paper Finalist Award at IROS 2023 (top 6%).

I'm eager to push the boundaries of perception in autonomous vehicles and robots and am enthusiastic about opportunities that allow me to apply my skills towards meaningful real-world impact. Let's connect and explore possibilities for collaboration and advancement.

positions.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellow
positions.description:
𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗨𝗔𝗩 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
• Developed an online self-supervised thermal water segmentation network capable of real-time adaptation, enabling nighttime river navigation capabilities without needing any thermal data prior to deployment. 
• Created an unsupervised RGB-to-thermal domain adaptation method using domain-specific attention modules and adversarial training to train a thermal semantic segmentation network without needing labels for thermal imagery nor paired RGB-thermal images.
• Enabled incremental supervised training for our UAV's semantic perception model by developing a fast and free method to generate semantic segmentation annotations for captured aerial thermal images using satellite data and visual foundation models.
• Created the first RGB-thermal (RGB-T) natural scenes dataset for aerial field robotics and developed new benchmarks for thermal/RGB-T semantic segmentation, RGB-T image translation, and thermal visual-inertial odometry and SLAM.

𝗠𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗱𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴
• Developed an RGB-thermal object detection algorithm for self-driving cars that fuses pretrained single-modality networks with minimal finetuning while outperforming other contemporary methods on various RGB-T object detection benchmarks.

𝗩𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻-𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗻𝗮𝘃𝗶𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘃𝗲𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀
• Developed a weakly-supervised image transform that increased localization match rate of existing image-registration-based visual navigation pipelines by over 20% in challenging cross-seasonal conditions. 
• Introduced a self-supervised method to discover and utilize optimal landmarks for efficient vision-based UAV navigation, requiring only 200 Mb of onboard storage to localize within a 150 sq. km. area.
positions.insights: Skills: Computer Vision · PyTorch · Python · Machine Learning · Robotics

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Improved efficiency of visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and mapping for augmented reality devices by 9% by developing an adaptive keyframe selection algorithm incorporating visual, motion, temporal, and state uncertainty information.
positions.insights: Skills: Visual SLAM · C++ · Visual Inertial Odometry · Computer Vision · Augmented Reality (AR)

positions.title: AI/ML Engineer
positions.description:
• Improved image deduplication model precision and recall for Siri Visual Intelligence using attention-based cropping augmentations, self-supervised contrastive representation learning, and deep ensemble methods. 
• Developed an adaptive, search-based thresholding algorithm to prune probable near-duplicate images in Siri web image search. Introduced in iOS 15.
positions.insights: Skills: Computer Vision · PyTorch · Distributed Systems · Python · Deep Learning

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Developed features in C# for Microsoft Graph and Active Directory to help app developers and owners manage identities and access. 
• Strengthened app security by developing a service action to automatically generate strong passwords during app creation, safeguarding users from potential security breaches.
• Introduced on-premises user extension attributes in MSGraph v1.0, enabling faster queries and seamless integration between on-premises and cloud infrastructure for customers like Sony, Costco, and Sainsbury.
positions.insights: Skills: C# · Software Design · Identity and Access Management (IAM)

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• CS156a: Learning From Data (introductory ML)
• CS156b: Learning Systems (recommendation systems)
positions.insights: Skills: Machine Learning · C++ · Python (Programming Language)

positions.title: Hannah Bradley Research Fellow
positions.description:
• Developed an entropy-based optimization algorithm to maximize visual features for visual simultaneous localization and mapping. 
• Integrated algorithm as a Python ROS package to enable quadrotor obstacle avoidance in forests with unstable lighting conditions.
positions.insights: Skills: Computer Vision · Visual SLAM · Robotics · Python · Robot Operating System (ROS)
